Indian Pale Male share ‘Law Abiding Citizen’ from forthcoming Great Satan Is Real EP

Manchester is full of genius poets and some exist just beyond the madding crowd. Nathan McIlroy fits the bill perfectly – a wild man of words with a political heart and soul he’s spent years delivering brilliance but now it feels like world has finally caught up with him.

indian Pale Male is his latest project and this song is a dark forest piano led ballad if a thin man and is as compellng and maverick as you hoped for.

Manchester newcomers Indian Pale Male have shared ‘Law Abiding Citizen’, the first track from their forthcoming EP Great Satan Is Real, due sometime before “the world ends” – which, by the band’s own reckoning, means circa 2026.

The new song arrives with an accompanying video, recorded live at Dead Basic Studios in Ancoats, and sets out the band’s stall in typically uncompromising fashion.

Watch ‘Law Abiding Citizen’ here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TEQiipn4Nks&list=RDTEQiipn4Nks&start_radio=1

The band say the song’s meaning is straightforward, boiling its message down to two blunt statements: “Genocide = bad” and “Preventing genocide = moral imperative.”

Great Satan Is Real will feature six tracks in total: Conversation Between the Sword and the Neck, Cruel Based Order, The Day After the Forever War, Free Speech Inc., Law Abiding Citizen and Apathetic Lament.

The titles alone hint at a band leaning hard into political unease, fractured public discourse and the darker mood of the times, but with enough gallows humour in the presentation to stop things becoming po-faced.

‘Law Abiding Citizen’ feels like a strong introduction: raw, direct and recorded with the kind of live edge that suits the song’s confrontational intent.

The group are also set to play their next show on 5 December at The Eagle Inn, supporting Piccadilly Rats as part of a late-afternoon Christmas bill.
